claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
Pre-oxidation at 900°C and approximately 0.1 atm O2 for 2–5 hours will create an ultrathin oxide scale.
The oxide scale produced by the proposed pre-oxidation treatment will be adherent.
Lower oxygen partial pressure produces a much thinner oxide scale and a lower oxidation rate in CrMnFeCoNi than oxidation at higher oxygen partial pressure.
The pre-formed ultrathin oxide scale will remain effective as a diffusion barrier during a subsequent 200-hour exposure at 900°C and 1 atm O2.
The pre-formed scale will moderate oxygen ingress during subsequent oxidation.
Providing a controlled pre-formed interface will reduce interfacial stresses.
Reduced oxygen ingress and interfacial stress will slow further oxide growth.
Reduced oxygen ingress and interfacial stress will mitigate scale spallation and microcrack formation.
Pre-treated specimens will exhibit slower oxidation kinetics and thinner, more uniform scales than untreated specimens.
Pre-treated specimens will exhibit better scale adhesion and fewer microstructural defects than untreated specimens.
Untreated CrMnFeCoNi undergoes vigorous oxidation in air or 1 atm oxygen at high temperature.
Untreated CrMnFeCoNi at 900°C and 1 atm O2 develops significant scale thickening, spallation, and defect formation.
The proposed behavior should hold around 900°C at oxygen partial pressures typical of industrial applications.
Applicability under extreme thermal cycling or substantially different oxygen partial pressures is uncertain.
Long-term stability and adherence of the pre-formed scale, especially under cyclic conditions, are uncertain and may depend on optimization of the pre-oxidation parameters.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in scale thickness, spallation, or defect formation relative to an untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
